question: Does a deployed strong choice have a provably inferior value to an alternative?
corpus: 8 original games plus 32 existing conditional continuations; no new policy experiment
screen: all idle move roots within last 3 decisions or both sides one survivor
bounds: one-step exact chance partition, unfinished mass unknown; existing full-information bound solver 1 second / 20000 executions per root
interpretation: full-information stochastic game, all opposing legal replies, optimal continuation; ties score 0.5. Pure win probabilities separately in terminal mass.
acceptance: positive lower bound on selected action loss or alternative lower bound greater than selected upper bound; floating-point margin 1e-8
limitation: native engine requires recorded state and PRNG parity; this is not exhaustive native/deployed equivalence or a blind information-set proof

stages.name: screen
stages.selection: all idle move roots within last 3 decisions or both sides one survivor

stages.name: wide
stages.selection: all remaining idle move roots of original 8 games, plus baseline trial4 and trial12 turn500

stages.name: focus
stages.selection: original g4 turns10/53 and baseline trial4/trial12 turn500; same states, not additional independent roots
